top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 112, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Ring of Kerry Charity Cycle's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
52ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Ring of Kerry Charity Cycle. Practice on paved Irish roads circumnavigating the Iveragh: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 112 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Ring of Kerry Charity Cycle. Train it until it feels boring.
At Ring of Kerry Charity Cycle, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,774ft of climbing on paved Irish roads circumnavigating the Iveragh does to your power file on race day.
5,774ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
112 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 112 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 112 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Tempo is Ring of Kerry Charity Cycle's race pace. The wattage you'll hold for 112 miles on paved Irish roads circumnavigating the Iveragh. Train it until it's automatic.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Ring of Kerry Charity Cycle’s 112 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 112 miles of paved irish roads circumnavigating the iveragh peninsula in Killarney, County Kerry, Ireland.
